My name is Leonard Hayes and I'm the CEO and co-founder of harmonygames.

I’m reaching out because we are shutting down Harmony Games, Inc. and want
to make sure we execute an orderly wind-down properly.

We are a Delaware corporation, qualified to do business in North Carolina
and California. We have preferred stock from a seed round (no SAFEs). We
have no US employees other than ourselves and only 4 international
contractors. We are out of funds and want to avoid missteps around creditor
ha[USERNAME_11664], state Withdrawals, tax filings, and closing operational accounts
cleanly.

We are looking for help with a managed wind-down, including:

   -

   A practical wind-down plan and timeline
   -

   Vendor termination support
   -

   Creditor communications and claim handling approach
   -

   Delaware dissolution and withdrawals in CA and NC, plus tax/accounting
   closeout coordination
   -

   Guidance on reserves and any final distributions consistent with
   preferred stock terms

If this is in your wheelhouse, can we set up a short call this week? I can
share our current cash position, liabilities list, and key contracts in
advance.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes"}}}, {"id": "robert@harmonygames.co/<CH2PR15MB3558F3E72D36311458EEB4BCDE62A@CH2PR15MB3558.namprd15.prod.outlook.com>", "threadId": "robert@harmonygames.co/1856689465442954434", "labelIds": ["SPAM", "CATEGORY_PERSONAL", "UNREAD"], "snippet": "Hello Leonard, Pleasure to meet you here via email. input.title: Combo Fighter — Honest Wind-Down Account (for angel calls) — Feb 2026
input.bodyText:
COMBO FIGHTER — AN HONEST ACCOUNT
Prepared by Robert (Co-Founder / Creative Director) — 28 Feb 2026
For: Leonard's angel conversations. Written from the primary data, not from memory or pasted screenshots.

WHY THIS EXISTS
Combo Fighter was my design — the difficulty curve, the card economy, all of it. If we are going to tell people the game ended "because of what the data showed," then the data should be written down honestly by the person who owned it, before our accounts go dark. What follows is the real record, pulled from the Snowflake warehouse (ANALYTICS + FINANCE) and the wind-down channel. I have not smoothed the bad parts or inflated the good ones.

=====================================================================
1) HOW COMBO FIGHTER ACTUALLY PERFORMED
=====================================================================
Player-facing life: 5 Jan 2026 – 9 Feb 2026 (36 days of live player data; the analytics window closes 9 Feb, the day we decided to stop). Paid acquisition actually ran 5 Jan – 28 Feb (see section 4 — it was never turned off).

Engagement (source: ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS, iOS+Android):
- DAU grew every single week: ~45 combined DAU on day one (5 Jan) to ~783 on 9 Feb. Peak ~784 (8 Feb). Roughly a 17x ramp in five weeks with almost no marketing muscle behind it.
- Lifetime sessions: 55,101. Average session length: 12.7 minutes — long for a casual prototype.
- Retention (daily average across the life of the game): D1 44.0%, D7 22.1%, D30 11.0%. D1 ranged 37–51%.

The benchmark that matters: our shipped title, Zombie Match 3D, was running D1 retention UNDER 30% — and the Jan 2026 board report cites that sub-30% D1 as a key reason for the shutdown decision. Combo Fighter's D1 ran ~14 points HIGHER than the game we were betting the company on. On the single metric we said we were killing games over, the prototype beat the flagship.

Install mix (source: INSTALL_EVENTS sample): roughly 54% of installs were ORGANIC. For a prototype with a few thousand dollars of ad spend, better than half the players arriving on their own is a real signal, not noise.

The honest downside — I am not going to hide it:
- Revenue was $0. Zero IAP, zero ad revenue, zero paying users (source: MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY). By design it was a prototype and the card economy was never switched over to monetize — but the plain fact is it never earned a cent, so we have retention signal and no proof it could pay for itself.
- Absolute scale was still tiny: sub-800 DAU, ~845 first-seen active users across the window.
- Install-to-active was soft: 1,341 paid installs produced only ~845 total new actives — a meaningful chunk of the installs we paid for never really showed up.
- It only lived five weeks. Strong early curves can still bend.

The truthful one-line read: Combo Fighter was a healthy, growing, sticky prototype that was killed by our bank balance, not by its own numbers. The data on the GAME read better than the data on the COMPANY. That is the honest version, and it is a better story than the soft one.

=====================================================================
2) WHAT WE PAID TO PUT PLAYERS IN FRONT OF IT (UA)
=====================================================================
Source: ANALYTICS.MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY. Lifetime paid UA (5 Jan – 28 Feb):
- Total spend: $7,476
- Paid installs: 1,341
- Blended CPI: $5.57

By channel:
- Meta / Facebook:  $2,265  (426 installs)
- Meta / Instagram: $1,351  (236 installs)
- Unity Ads:        $1,318  (241 installs)
- Google UAC:       $1,068  (191 installs)
- ironSource:         $742  (122 installs)
- AppLovin:           $732  (125 installs)

Read it straight: ~$5.57 to buy a player against $0 of realized revenue. On a pure return basis every acquired user was a loss, because we never monetized. That is normal for a prototype UA test — you are buying signal, not payback — but nobody should tell an angel that Combo Fighter "worked economically." It proved engagement, not unit economics.

=====================================================================
3) WHAT IS STILL QUIETLY COSTING US (the live leak)
=====================================================================
THE ONE THAT MATTERS — Combo Fighter paid UA was never switched off.
We decided to stop on 9 Feb. The ad campaigns did not:
- Spend AFTER 9 Feb (10–28 Feb): $2,441 on 443 installs, still live and charging roughly $110/day (~$3,300/month run-rate) as of today, 28 Feb.
- It is invisible in the P&L: the February burn table (FINANCE) has salaries, legal, AWS, tools — but NO marketing line at all. When Leonard said "I looked at the P&L and I think this covers everything," the P&L literally cannot see this spend, because it sits on the ad networks, not in the accounting categories.
- The wind-down subscription checklist cancelled SaaS tools (Cursor, CodeRabbit, Soundly, Helpshift, layer, Zapier, etc.) and is terminating Unity and Singular — but it never listed the six ad campaigns (Meta FB/IG, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin). They fell through the gap.
ACTION: pause all six campaigns immediately. Every day we wait is ~$110 out of three founders' pockets. A tracking item has been filed (see below).

OTHER RETAINED / STILL-RUNNING COSTS (deliberately kept, per the wind-down channel):
- Metabase + dbt: ~$300/month total, moved to Arthur's KubLLC card, being kept ALIVE specifically so I can keep looking at Combo Fighter data. Worth naming plainly: the one analytics stack we're still paying for is being kept for me. If I'm done, say so and it goes.
- Gusto, Intuit (~2 more months), Deel — kept intentionally through shutdown for payroll/tax/doc access.
- GitHub, Slack, Google, Google Analytics — kept until the data is extracted/sold, then transferred.
- Linear — kept during the transition.
- Carta — renewal 15 Aug, tied to the (now-closing) Chase account; being left alone deliberately.
These are known and controlled. The UA leak is the one that was NOT known.

=====================================================================
4) THE MONEY — DOES THE DATA DEAL COVER AN ORDERLY SHUTDOWN?
=====================================================================
Be precise, because the number you (Robert) have been carrying is probably the gross, not the net.

The data deal (buyer = the "Sunset" data-licensing counterparty; Leonard's own figures, 12 Feb):
- Gross cash offer: $22,500
- Their charge to us: $11,700
- NET to Harmony Games: ~$10,800
(Structured as a data LICENSE, not an outright data sale, so we retain our IP.)

Cash on hand, 28 Feb (FINANCE.CASH_BALANCE): $2,500. (Jan close was $25K; we are effectively out of money.)

Obligations the net proceeds have to clear:
- SVB credit-card balance — the priority. Plan: as soon as the data cash lands, pay SVB in full and close the card.
- Unity Pro — seeking a $0 mutual termination on insolvency grounds (Arthur). Leonard is "not so hopeful" this one is free.
- Singular (MMP) — seeking a $0 mutual termination; a prior quarterly payment was already deferred (Leonard "high hopes").
- Helpshift — roughly $1,500 owed on the order form.
- Legal / managed wind-down — the single largest REAL cash cost: ~$13,000 in February alone (plus ~$5,000 in January).
- Leapblock contractor — ~$600–1,200 goodwill gesture (optional).

THE STRAIGHT ANSWER: it is marginal, not comfortable. The net data proceeds (~$10.8K) are roughly the size of ONE line item — the legal bill — and are essentially spoken for by paying off the SVB card. The wind-down only "balances" if Unity AND Singular both agree to walk away at $0 rather than demand payment, because there is no cash to pay them if they don't. There is no buffer. And it is being quietly eroded, right now, by the ~$110/day of UA we forgot to switch off. Leonard, Arthur and I are personally on the hook, so the honest framing is: "the data covers a clean, orderly shutdown — barely — and only if two vendors write off their balances and we stop the ad bleed today." Anything less and it comes out of our own pockets.

=====================================================================
5) THE 2–3 FIGURES TO LEAD WITH ON THE CALLS
=====================================================================
1. 44% D1 retention (peaking 51%) vs our shipped game's sub-30% — the design worked; the game was killed by cash, not by the curve.
2. ~780 DAU in 5 weeks at a $5.57 CPI, ~54% organic — and $0 revenue: real engagement, unproven economics. Be honest about both halves.
3. ~$10,800 net from the data deal against $2,500 cash and a ~$13,000 legal bill — the wind-down is being run tight and clean, and closes only if Unity + Singular write off and we cut the ~$110/day UA that's still running.

=====================================================================
SOURCES & METHOD
=====================================================================
- Snowflake ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS (DAU, sessions, retention), MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY (UA spend/CPI), MARKETING.INSTALL_EVENTS (organic mix), MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY (revenue = $0).
- Snowflake FINANCE.EXPENSES.CASH_BALANCE and MONTHLY_BURN (cash, legal, burn).
- Slack #winddown (data-deal figures, subscription/vendor status, SVB/Unity/Singular plan) and the wind-down advisor email thread.
- Combo Fighter design/GDD ownership: Robert.
All dollar figures are as recorded in the systems above as of 28 Feb 2026.

input.title: [Wind-down] Combo Fighter paid UA still live — kill all 6 ad campaigns (bleeding ~$110/day)
input.description:
## What
Combo Fighter paid user-acquisition campaigns were **never paused** when we decided to stop on 9 Feb 2026. They are still spending as of today (28 Feb).

## The figure
- Spend after the 9 Feb stop decision (10–28 Feb): **$2,441** on 443 installs.
- Current run-rate: **~$110/day (~$3,300/month)** and climbing.
- Lifetime Combo Fighter UA: $7,476 / 1,341 installs / $5.57 CPI. Revenue from the game: **$0**.
- **Not visible in the P&L** — the Feb finance burn table has no marketing line; this sits on the ad networks, so "the P&L covers everything" review missed it.

## Channels to turn off (all six)
Meta/Facebook, Meta/Instagram, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin.

## Why it matters
Leonard, Arthur and Robert are personally on the hook for the wind-down. Net proceeds from the data license are only ~$10.8K and are marginal against shutdown costs; every day this runs is founder cash. The subscription cancellation checklist covered SaaS tools but never listed the ad campaigns.

## Action
1. Pause/stop all six campaigns in each ad network dashboard immediately.
2. Confirm no further charges hit the card the campaigns bill to (note SVB card is being closed on data-cash receipt).
3. Reply here with confirmation + the final stopped-spend total.

## Owner
Arthur Blake (operational shutdown / vendor + card cancellations). Watchers: Leonard Hayes, Robert.

Source: Snowflake ANALYTICS.MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY (game_id='combo_fighter'); Slack #winddown. Full writeup: Google Doc "Combo Fighter — Honest Wind-Down Account".

<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> — I went back through the real numbers (Snowflake + this channel) instead of the screenshots, and wrote up one honest account for the angel calls. Full doc (owned by me, exportable so it outlasts our accounts): https://docs.google.com/document/d/9933969ce27924f22e067216/edit

Three things worth your time:

*1) Combo Fighter actually performed — it was killed by cash, not by its data.* Jan 5–Feb 9: DAU grew ~45 → ~780 in five weeks, avg session 12.7 min, D1 retention *44%* (peaked 51%). For context ZM3D's D1 was under 30% and the board cited that as a shutdown reason. The prototype beat the flagship on the metric we said we kill games over. Honest downsides: $0 revenue (never monetized), sub-800 DAU, only 5 weeks, and 1,341 paid installs only produced ~845 actives. Lifetime UA $7,476 @ $5.57 CPI.

*2) 🚨 Something is still bleeding: Combo Fighter paid UA was never switched off.* All six ad campaigns (Meta FB/IG, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin) are still live. *$2,441 spent Feb 10–28*, ~$110/day (~$3.3K/mo), and it's *not in the P&L* — it sits on the ad networks, not the accounting categories, which is why the P&L review didn't catch it. Filed <https://linear.app/harmonygames-games/issue/ENG-2438|ENG-2438> for <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> to kill all six today. (Separately: Metabase+dbt ~$300/mo is being kept alive on Arthur's card for *my* Combo Fighter data — if you two want that gone, I can let it go.)

*3) On whether the data covers an orderly shutdown — it's marginal, not comfortable.* Net from the data license is ~$10.8K ($22.5K gross − $11.7K), against $2.5K cash and a ~$13K Feb legal bill alone. It only balances if Unity *and* Singular both write off at $0 — there's no cash to pay them otherwise — and the UA leak above is quietly eating the margin. Leonard, the number to carry is the *net ~$10.8K*, not the $22.5K gross.

Details, channel splits and sources all in the doc. Yell if any figure looks off and I'll trace it back to the table.
